newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Komi republic says working on rating.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Komi republic says working on rating.

text.p: Russia's northern Komi Republic is seeking an international rating mainly to help local companies raise foreign credit, and plans for Komi to issue a Eurobond are of secondary importance, a senior official said.
"The question (of a rating) was raised to create normal conditions for private companies to get credit and increase their chances," Deputy Economy Minister Sergei Frolov told Reuters.
"Once we get the rating, then there will be something to talk about."

Earlier this year, senior Komi officials said the republic hoped to raise $200 million through a five-year Eurobond in 1997, but Frolov said such an issue would depend on permission from Moscow, as well as the rating and market conditions.

"Taking into account the success of those regions that have already placed Eurobonds, we would like to (issue a Eurobond)," he said, referring to launches by St Petersburg and Moscow city administrations.
"But we do not strictly link the goal to getting the rating. That would be jumping the gun."
He said investment bank SBC Warburg was working with the republic on receiving an international credit rating.

"SBC Warburg, which is acting as our consultant, has started work on gathering and preparing the documentation," Frolov said. "Then we will start work looking for a rating agency, which will be done on a tender basis."
Both Moscow and St Petersburg, as well as Nizhny Novgorod regional administration received permission to issue Eurobonds through a presidential decree giving conditions for the issue.
It is not clear whether and when a long list of other local authorities will be allowed to follow suit.
Sverdlovsk, Chelyabinsk, Samara, Perm and Irkutsk regions, as well as the Tatar and Sakha Republics have announced plans to issue Eurobonds.
